**** 4.1.3 Summary Buffer Mode Line [[#Summary-Buffer-Mode-Line-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Summary-Buffer-Mode-Line-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
You can also change the format of the summary mode bar (see
[[#Mode-Line-Formatting][Mode Line Formatting]]). Set
=gnus-summary-mode-line-format= to whatever you like. The default is
‘=Gnus: %%b [%A] %Z='.

Here are the elements you can play with:

- ‘=G=' :: Group name.

- ‘=p=' :: Unprefixed group name.

- ‘=A=' :: Current article number.

- ‘=z=' :: Current article score.

- ‘=V=' :: Gnus version.

- ‘=U=' :: Number of unread articles in this group.

- ‘=e=' :: Number of unread articles in this group that aren't displayed
  in the summary buffer.

- ‘=Z=' :: A string with the number of unread and unselected articles
  represented either as ‘=<%U(+%e) more>=' if there are both unread and
  unselected articles, and just as ‘=<%U more>=' if there are just
  unread articles and no unselected ones.

- ‘=g=' :: Shortish group name. For instance, ‘=rec.arts.anime=' will be
  shortened to ‘=r.a.anime='.

- ‘=S=' :: Subject of the current article.

- ‘=u=' :: User-defined spec (see
  [[#User_002dDefined-Specs][User-Defined Specs]]).

- ‘=s=' :: Name of the current score file (see [[#Scoring][Scoring]]).

- ‘=d=' :: Number of dormant articles (see
  [[#Unread-Articles][Unread Articles]]).

- ‘=t=' :: Number of ticked articles (see
  [[#Unread-Articles][Unread Articles]]).

- ‘=r=' :: Number of articles that have been marked as read in this
  session.

- ‘=E=' :: Number of articles expunged by the score files.

--------------

<<Summary-Highlighting>>

**** 4.1.4 Summary Highlighting [[#Summary-Highlighting-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Summary-Highlighting-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
- <<index-gnus_002dvisual_002dmark_002darticle_002dhook>>=gnus-visual-mark-article-hook=
  [[#index-gnus_002dvisual_002dmark_002darticle_002dhook][¶]] :: This
  hook is run after selecting an article. It is meant to be used for
  highlighting the article in some way. It is not run if =gnus-visual=
  is =nil=.

- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dupdate_002dhook>>=gnus-summary-update-hook=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dupdate_002dhook][¶]] :: This hook is
  called when a summary line is changed. It is not run if =gnus-visual=
  is =nil=.

- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dselected_002dface>>=gnus-summary-selected-face=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dselected_002dface][¶]] :: This is the
  face (or /font/ as some people call it) used to highlight the current
  article in the summary buffer.

- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dhighlight>>=gnus-summary-highlight=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dhighlight][¶]] :: Summary lines are
  highlighted according to this variable, which is a list where the
  elements are of the format =(==form== . ==face==)=. If you would, for
  instance, like ticked articles to be italic and high-scored articles
  to be bold, you could set this variable to something like

  #+begin_src lisp-preformatted
  (((eq mark gnus-ticked-mark) . italic)
   ((> score default) . bold))
  #+end_src

  As you may have guessed, if =form= returns a non-=nil= value, =face=
  will be applied to the line.

*** 4.2 Summary Maneuvering [[#Summary-Maneuvering-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Summary-Maneuvering-1
:CLASS: section
:END:
All the straight movement commands understand the numeric prefix and
behave pretty much as you'd expect.

None of these commands select articles.

-  <<index-M_002dn-_0028Summary_0029>>G M-n
  [[#index-M_002dn-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  M-n :: Go to the next summary line of an unread article
  (=gnus-summary-next-unread-subject=).

-  <<index-M_002dp-_0028Summary_0029>>G M-p
  [[#index-M_002dp-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  M-p :: Go to the previous summary line of an unread article
  (=gnus-summary-prev-unread-subject=).

-  <<index-G-g-_0028Summary_0029>>G g
  [[#index-G-g-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Ask for an article number and
  then go to the summary line of that article without displaying the
  article (=gnus-summary-goto-subject=).

If Gnus asks you to press a key to confirm going to the next group, you
can use the C-n and C-p keys to move around the group buffer, searching
for the next group to read without actually returning to the group
buffer.

Variables related to summary movement:

- <<index-gnus_002dauto_002dselect_002dnext>>=gnus-auto-select-next=
  [[#index-gnus_002dauto_002dselect_002dnext][¶]] :: If you issue one of
  the movement commands (like n) and there are no more unread articles
  after the current one, Gnus will offer to go to the next group. If
  this variable is =t= and the next group is empty, Gnus will exit
  summary mode and return to the group buffer. If this variable is
  neither =t= nor =nil=, Gnus will select the next group with unread
  articles. As a special case, if this variable is =quietly=, Gnus will
  select the next group without asking for confirmation. If this
  variable is =almost-quietly=, the same will happen only if you are
  located on the last article in the group. Finally, if this variable is
  =slightly-quietly=, the Z n command will go to the next group without
  confirmation. Also see [[#Group-Levels][Group Levels]].

- <<index-gnus_002dauto_002dselect_002dsame>>=gnus-auto-select-same=
  [[#index-gnus_002dauto_002dselect_002dsame][¶]] :: If non-=nil=, all
  the movement commands will try to go to the next article with the same
  subject as the current. (/Same/ here might mean /roughly equal/. See
  =gnus-summary-gather-subject-limit= for details (see
  [[#Customizing-Threading][Customizing Threading]]).) If there are no
  more articles with the same subject, go to the first unread article.

  This variable is not particularly useful if you use a threaded
  display.

- <<index-gnus_002dpaging_002dselect_002dnext>>=gnus-paging-select-next=
  [[#index-gnus_002dpaging_002dselect_002dnext][¶]] :: Control whether
  to select the next/previous article when paging (with commands like
  SPC or DEL). If non-=nil=, select the next article when reaching the
  end of the article (or the previous article when paging backwards).

  If =nil=, don't do anything at the end/start of the articles.

- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dcheck_002dcurrent>>=gnus-summary-check-current=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dcheck_002dcurrent][¶]] :: If non-=nil=,
  all the “unread” movement commands will not proceed to the next (or
  previous) article if the current article is unread. Instead, they will
  choose the current article.

- <<index-gnus_002dauto_002dcenter_002dsummary>>=gnus-auto-center-summary=
  [[#index-gnus_002dauto_002dcenter_002dsummary][¶]] :: If non-=nil=,
  Gnus will keep the point in the summary buffer centered at all times.
  This makes things quite tidy, but if you have a slow network
  connection, or simply do not like this un-Emacsism, you can set this
  variable to =nil= to get the normal Emacs scrolling action. This will
  also inhibit horizontal re-centering of the summary buffer, which
  might make it more inconvenient to read extremely long threads.

  This variable can also be a number. In that case, center the window at
  the given number of lines from the top.

- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dstop_002dat_002dend_002dof_002dmessage>>=gnus-summary-stop-at-end-of-message=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dstop_002dat_002dend_002dof_002dmessage][¶]] :: If
  non-=nil=, don't go to the next article when hitting SPC, and you're
  at the end of the article.

**** 4.3.1 Choosing Commands [[#Choosing-Commands-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Choosing-Commands-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
None of the following movement commands understand the numeric prefix,
and they all select and display an article.

If you want to fetch new articles or redisplay the group, see
[[#Exiting-the-Summary-Buffer][Exiting the Summary Buffer]].

-  <<index-SPC-_0028Summary_0029>>SPC
  [[#index-SPC-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Select the current article, or,
  if that one's read already, the next unread article
  (=gnus-summary-next-page=).

  If you have an article window open already and you press SPC again,
  the article will be scrolled. This lets you conveniently SPC through
  an entire newsgroup. See
  [[#Paging-the-Article][Scrolling the Article]].

-  <<index-n-_0028Summary_0029>>G n [[#index-n-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  n :: Go to next unread article (=gnus-summary-next-unread-article=).

-  <<index-p-_0028Summary_0029>>G p [[#index-p-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  p :: Go to previous unread article
  (=gnus-summary-prev-unread-article=).

-  <<index-N-_0028Summary_0029>>G N [[#index-N-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  N :: Go to the next article (=gnus-summary-next-article=).

-  <<index-P-_0028Summary_0029>>G P [[#index-P-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  P :: Go to the previous article (=gnus-summary-prev-article=).

-  <<index-_005d-_0028Summary_0029>>G u
  [[#index-_005d-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  ] :: Go to the next unseen article
  (=gnus-summary-next-unseen-article=).

-  <<index-_005b-_0028Summary_0029>>G U
  [[#index-_005b-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  [ :: Go to the previous unseen article
  (=gnus-summary-prev-unseen-article=).

-  <<index-G-C_002dn-_0028Summary_0029>>G C-n
  [[#index-G-C_002dn-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Go to the next article
  with the same subject (=gnus-summary-next-same-subject=).

-  <<index-G-C_002dp-_0028Summary_0029>>G C-p
  [[#index-G-C_002dp-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Go to the previous
  article with the same subject (=gnus-summary-prev-same-subject=).

-  <<index-G-f-_0028Summary_0029>>G f
  [[#index-G-f-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  . :: Go to the first unread article
  (=gnus-summary-first-unread-article=).

-  <<index-G-b-_0028Summary_0029>>G b
  [[#index-G-b-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  , :: Go to the unread article with the highest score
  (=gnus-summary-best-unread-article=). If given a prefix argument, go
  to the first unread article that has a score over the default score.

-  <<index-l-_0028Summary_0029>>G l [[#index-l-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  l :: Go to the previous article read
  (=gnus-summary-goto-last-article=).

-  <<index-G-o-_0028Summary_0029>>G o
  [[#index-G-o-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Pop an article off the summary
  history and go to this article (=gnus-summary-pop-article=). This
  command differs from the command above in that you can pop as many
  previous articles off the history as you like, while l toggles the two
  last read articles. For a somewhat related issue (if you use these
  commands a lot), see [[#Article-Backlog][Article Backlog]].

-  <<index-j-_0028Summary_0029>>G j [[#index-j-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  j :: Ask for an article number or =Message-ID=, and then go to that
  article (=gnus-summary-goto-article=).

**** 4.3.2 Choosing Variables [[#Choosing-Variables-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Choosing-Variables-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
Some variables relevant for moving and selecting articles:

- <<index-gnus_002dauto_002dextend_002dnewsgroup>>=gnus-auto-extend-newsgroup=
  [[#index-gnus_002dauto_002dextend_002dnewsgroup][¶]] :: All the
  movement commands will try to go to the previous (or next) article,
  even if that article isn't displayed in the Summary buffer if this
  variable is non-=nil=. Gnus will then fetch the article from the
  server and display it in the article buffer.

- <<index-gnus_002dselect_002darticle_002dhook>>=gnus-select-article-hook=
  [[#index-gnus_002dselect_002darticle_002dhook][¶]] :: This hook is
  called whenever an article is selected. The default is =nil=. If you
  would like each article to be saved in the Agent as you read it,
  putting =gnus-agent-fetch-selected-article= on this hook will do so.

-  <<index-gnus_002dmark_002darticle_002dhook>>=gnus-mark-article-hook=
  [[#index-gnus_002dmark_002darticle_002dhook][¶]] :: This hook is
  called whenever an article is selected. It is intended to be used for
  marking articles as read. The default value is
  =gnus-summary-mark-read-and-unread-as-read=, and will change the mark
  of almost any article you read to =gnus-read-mark=. The only articles
  not affected by this function are ticked, dormant, and expirable
  articles. If you'd instead like to just have unread articles marked as
  read, you can use =gnus-summary-mark-unread-as-read= instead. It will
  leave marks like =gnus-low-score-mark=, =gnus-del-mark= (and so on)
  alone.

*** 4.4 Scrolling the Article [[#Scrolling-the-Article][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Scrolling-the-Article
:CLASS: section
:END:
-  <<index-SPC-_0028Summary_0029-1>>SPC
  [[#index-SPC-_0028Summary_0029-1][¶]] :: Pressing SPC will scroll the
  current article forward one page, or, if you have come to the end of
  the current article, will choose the next article
  (=gnus-summary-next-page=).

  If =gnus-article-skip-boring= is non-=nil= and the rest of the article
  consists only of citations and signature, then it will be skipped; the
  next article will be shown instead. You can customize what is
  considered uninteresting with =gnus-article-boring-faces=. You can
  manually view the article's pages, no matter how boring, using C-M-v.

-  <<index-DEL-_0028Summary_0029>>DEL
  [[#index-DEL-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Scroll the current article back
  one page (=gnus-summary-prev-page=).

-  <<index-RET-_0028Summary_0029>>RET
  [[#index-RET-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Scroll the current article one
  line forward (=gnus-summary-scroll-up=).

-  <<index-M_002dRET-_0028Summary_0029>>M-RET
  [[#index-M_002dRET-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Scroll the current
  article one line backward (=gnus-summary-scroll-down=).

-  <<index-A-g-_0028Summary_0029>>A g
  [[#index-A-g-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  g :: (Re)fetch the current article (=gnus-summary-show-article=). If
  given a prefix, show a completely “raw” article, just the way it came
  from the server. If given a prefix twice (i.e., C-u C-u g'), fetch the
  current article, but don't run any of the article treatment functions.

  If given a numerical prefix, you can do semi-manual charset stuff. C-u
  0 g cn-gb-2312 RET will decode the message as if it were encoded in
  the =cn-gb-2312= charset. If you have

  #+begin_src lisp-preformatted
  (setq gnus-summary-show-article-charset-alist
        '((1 . cn-gb-2312)
          (2 . big5)))
  #+end_src

  then you can say C-u 1 g to get the same effect.

-  <<index-_003c-_0028Summary_0029>>A <
  [[#index-_003c-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  < :: Scroll to the beginning of the article
  (=gnus-summary-beginning-of-article=).

-  <<index-_003e-_0028Summary_0029>>A >
  [[#index-_003e-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  > :: Scroll to the end of the article (=gnus-summary-end-of-article=).

-  <<index-A-s-_0028Summary_0029>>A s
  [[#index-A-s-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  s :: Perform an isearch in the article buffer
  (=gnus-summary-isearch-article=).

-  <<index-h-_0028Summary_0029>>h
  [[#index-h-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Select the article buffer
  (=gnus-summary-select-article-buffer=).

**** 4.5.1 Summary Mail Commands [[#Summary-Mail-Commands-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Summary-Mail-Commands-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
Commands for composing a mail message:

-  <<index-S-r-_0028Summary_0029>>S r
  [[#index-S-r-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  r :: Mail a reply to the author of the current article
  (=gnus-summary-reply=).

-  <<index-R-_0028Summary_0029>>S R [[#index-R-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  R :: Mail a reply to the author of the current article and include the
  original message (=gnus-summary-reply-with-original=). This command
  uses the process/prefix convention.

-  <<index-S-w-_0028Summary_0029>>S w
  [[#index-S-w-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mail a wide reply to the author
  of the current article (=gnus-summary-wide-reply=). A /wide reply/ is
  a reply that goes out to all people listed in the =To=, =From= (or
  =Reply-To=) and =Cc= headers. If =Mail-Followup-To= is present, that's
  used instead.

-  <<index-S-W-_0028Summary_0029>>S W
  [[#index-S-W-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mail a wide reply to the
  current article and include the original message
  (=gnus-summary-wide-reply-with-original=). This command uses the
  process/prefix convention, but only uses the headers from the first
  article to determine the recipients.

-  <<index-S-L-_0028Summary_0029>>S L
  [[#index-S-L-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: When replying to a message from
  a mailing list, send a reply to that message to the mailing list, and
  include the original message
  (=gnus-summary-reply-to-list-with-original=).

-  <<index-S-v-_0028Summary_0029>>S v
  [[#index-S-v-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mail a very wide reply to the
  author of the current article (=gnus-summary-very-wide-reply=). A
  /very wide reply/ is a reply that goes out to all people listed in the
  =To=, =From= (or =Reply-To=) and =Cc= headers in all the
  process/prefixed articles. This command uses the process/prefix
  convention. If given a prefix argument, the body of the current
  article will also be yanked.

-  <<index-S-V-_0028Summary_0029>>S V
  [[#index-S-V-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mail a very wide reply to the
  author of the current article and include the original message
  (=gnus-summary-very-wide-reply-with-original=). This command uses the
  process/prefix convention.

-  <<index-S-B-r-_0028Summary_0029>>S B r
  [[#index-S-B-r-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mail a reply to the author of
  the current article but ignore the =Reply-To= field
  (=gnus-summary-reply-broken-reply-to=). If you need this because a
  mailing list incorrectly sets a =Reply-To= header pointing to the
  list, you probably want to set the =broken-reply-to= group parameter
  instead, so things will work correctly. See
  [[#Group-Parameters][Group Parameters]].

-  <<index-S-B-R-_0028Summary_0029>>S B R
  [[#index-S-B-R-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mail a reply to the author of
  the current article and include the original message but ignore the
  =Reply-To= field (=gnus-summary-reply-broken-reply-to-with-original=).

-  <<index-S-o-m-_0028Summary_0029>>S o m
  [[#index-S-o-m-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  C-c C-f :: Forward the current article to some other person
  (=gnus-summary-mail-forward=). If no prefix is given, the message is
  forwarded according to the value of (=message-forward-as-mime=) and
  (=message-forward-show-mml=); if the prefix is 1, decode the message
  and forward directly inline; if the prefix is 2, forward message as an
  rfc822 MIME section; if the prefix is 3, decode message and forward as
  an rfc822 MIME section; if the prefix is 4, forward message directly
  inline; otherwise, the message is forwarded as no prefix given but use
  the negated value of (=message-forward-as-mime=). By default, the
  forwarded message is inlined into the mail.

  Which headers from the original message are included in the forwarded
  message is determined by options specific to =message-mode=, see
  [[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_mono/message.html#Forwarding][(message)Forwarding]].
  In addition, this command can be given the symbolic prefix ‘=a=',
  using M-i a, to include most original headers.

-  <<index-m-_0028Summary_0029>>S m [[#index-m-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  m :: Prepare a mail (=gnus-summary-mail-other-window=). By default,
  use the posting style of the current group. If given a prefix, disable
  that. If the prefix is 1, prompt for a group name to find the posting
  style.

-  <<index-S-i-_0028Summary_0029>>S i
  [[#index-S-i-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Prepare a news
  (=gnus-summary-news-other-window=). By default, post to the current
  group. If given a prefix, disable that. If the prefix is 1, prompt for
  a group to post to.

  This function actually prepares a news even when using mail groups.
  This is useful for “posting” messages to mail groups without actually
  sending them over the network: they're just saved directly to the
  group in question. The corresponding back end must have a request-post
  method for this to work though.

-  <<index-S-D-b-_0028Summary_0029>>S D b
  [[#index-S-D-b-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: If you have sent a mail, but
  the mail was bounced back to you for some reason (wrong address,
  transient failure), you can use this command to resend that bounced
  mail (=gnus-summary-resend-bounced-mail=). You will be popped into a
  mail buffer where you can edit the headers before sending the mail off
  again. If you give a prefix to this command, and the bounced mail is a
  reply to some other mail, Gnus will try to fetch that mail and display
  it for easy perusal of its headers. This might very well fail, though.

-  <<index-S-D-r-_0028Summary_0029>>S D r
  [[#index-S-D-r-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Not to be confused with the
  previous command, =gnus-summary-resend-message= will prompt you for an
  address to send the current message off to, and then send it to that
  place. The headers of the message won't be altered---but lots of
  headers that say =Resent-To=, =Resent-From= and so on will be added.
  This means that you actually send a mail to someone that has a =To=
  header that (probably) points to yourself. This will confuse people.
  So, natcherly you'll only do that if you're really eVIl.

  This command is mainly used if you have several accounts and want to
  ship a mail to a different account of yours. (If you're both =root=
  and =postmaster= and get a mail for =postmaster= to the =root=
  account, you may want to resend it to =postmaster=. Ordnung muss sein!

  This command understands the process/prefix convention (see
  [[#Process_002fPrefix][Process/Prefix]]).

-  <<index-S-D-e-_0028Summary_0029>>S D e
  [[#index-S-D-e-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Like the previous command,
  but will allow you to edit the message as if it were a new message
  before resending.

-  <<index-S-O-m-_0028Summary_0029>>S O m
  [[#index-S-O-m-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Digest the current series
  (see [[#Decoding-Articles][Decoding Articles]]) and forward the result
  using mail (=gnus-uu-digest-mail-forward=). This command uses the
  process/prefix convention (see
  [[#Process_002fPrefix][Process/Prefix]]).

-  <<index-S-M_002dc-_0028Summary_0029>>S M-c
  [[#index-S-M_002dc-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Send a complaint about
  excessive crossposting to the author of the current article
  (=gnus-summary-mail-crosspost-complaint=).

  This command is provided as a way to fight back against the current
  crossposting pandemic that's sweeping Usenet. It will compose a reply
  using the =gnus-crosspost-complaint= variable as a preamble. This
  command understands the process/prefix convention (see
  [[#Process_002fPrefix][Process/Prefix]]) and will prompt you before
  sending each mail.

Also See
[[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_mono/message.html#Header-Commands][Header Commands]]
in The Message Manual, for more information.

**** 4.5.2 Summary Post Commands [[#Summary-Post-Commands-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Summary-Post-Commands-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
Commands for posting a news article:

-  <<index-a-_0028Summary_0029>>S p [[#index-a-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  a :: Prepare for posting an article (=gnus-summary-post-news=). By
  default, post to the current group. If given a prefix, disable that.
  If the prefix is 1, prompt for another group instead.

-  <<index-f-_0028Summary_0029>>S f [[#index-f-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  f :: Post a followup to the current article (=gnus-summary-followup=).

-  <<index-S-F-_0028Summary_0029>>S F
  [[#index-S-F-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  F ::

  Post a followup to the current article and include the original
  message (=gnus-summary-followup-with-original=). This command uses the
  process/prefix convention.

-  <<index-S-n-_0028Summary_0029>>S n
  [[#index-S-n-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Post a followup to the current
  article via news, even if you got the message through mail
  (=gnus-summary-followup-to-mail=).

-  <<index-S-N-_0028Summary_0029>>S N
  [[#index-S-N-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Post a followup to the current
  article via news, even if you got the message through mail and include
  the original message (=gnus-summary-followup-to-mail-with-original=).
  This command uses the process/prefix convention.

-  <<index-S-o-p-_0028Summary_0029>>S o p
  [[#index-S-o-p-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Forward the current article
  to a newsgroup (=gnus-summary-post-forward=). If no prefix is given,
  the message is forwarded according to the value of
  (=message-forward-as-mime=) and (=message-forward-show-mml=); if the
  prefix is 1, decode the message and forward directly inline; if the
  prefix is 2, forward message as an rfc822 MIME section; if the prefix
  is 3, decode message and forward as an rfc822 MIME section; if the
  prefix is 4, forward message directly inline; otherwise, the message
  is forwarded as no prefix given but use the flipped value of
  (=message-forward-as-mime=). By default, the message is decoded and
  forwarded as an rfc822 MIME section.

-  <<index-S-O-p-_0028Summary_0029>>S O p
  [[#index-S-O-p-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Digest the current series and
  forward the result to a newsgroup (=gnus-uu-digest-post-forward=).
  This command uses the process/prefix convention.

-  <<index-S-u-_0028Summary_0029>>S u
  [[#index-S-u-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Uuencode a file, split it into
  parts, and post it as a series (=gnus-uu-post-news=). (see
  [[#Uuencoding-and-Posting][Uuencoding and Posting]]).

Also See
[[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_mono/message.html#Header-Commands][Header Commands]]
in The Message Manual, for more information.

**** 4.5.3 Summary Message Commands [[#Summary-Message-Commands-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Summary-Message-Commands-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
-  <<index-S-y-_0028Summary_0029>>S y
  [[#index-S-y-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Yank the current article into
  an already existing Message composition buffer
  (=gnus-summary-yank-message=). This command prompts for what message
  buffer you want to yank into, and understands the process/prefix
  convention (see [[#Process_002fPrefix][Process/Prefix]]).

-  <<index-S-A-_0028Summary_0029>>S A
  [[#index-S-A-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Attach the current article into
  an already existing Message composition buffer
  (=gnus-summary-attach-message=). If no such buffer exists, a new one
  is created. This command prompts for what message buffer you want to
  yank into, and understands the process/prefix convention (see
  [[#Process_002fPrefix][Process/Prefix]]).

**** 4.5.4 Canceling Articles [[#Canceling-Articles][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Canceling-Articles
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
Have you ever written something, and then decided that you really,
really, really wish you hadn't posted that?

Well, you can't cancel mail, but you can cancel posts.

Find the article you wish to cancel (you can only cancel your own
articles, so don't try any funny stuff). Then press C or S c
(=gnus-summary-cancel-article=). Your article will be
canceled---machines all over the world will be deleting your article.
This command uses the process/prefix convention (see
[[#Process_002fPrefix][Process/Prefix]]).

Be aware, however, that not all sites honor cancels, so your article may
live on here and there, while most sites will delete the article in
question.

Gnus will use the “current” select method when canceling. If you want to
use the standard posting method, use the ‘=a=' symbolic prefix (see
[[#Symbolic-Prefixes][Symbolic Prefixes]]).

Gnus ensures that only you can cancel your own messages using a
=Cancel-Lock= header (see
[[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_mono/message.html#Canceling-News][Canceling News]]
in Message Manual).

If you discover that you have made some mistakes and want to do some
corrections, you can post a /superseding/ article that will replace your
original article.

Go to the original article and press S s
(=gnus-summary-supersede-article=). You will be put in a buffer where
you can edit the article all you want before sending it off the usual
way.

The same goes for superseding as for canceling, only more so: Some sites
do not honor superseding. On those sites, it will appear that you have
posted almost the same article twice.

If you have just posted the article, and change your mind right away,
there is a trick you can use to cancel/supersede the article without
waiting for the article to appear on your site first. You simply return
to the post buffer (which is called =*sent ...*=). There you will find
the article you just posted, with all the headers intact. Change the
=Message-ID= header to a =Cancel= or =Supersedes= header by substituting
one of those words for the word =Message-ID=. Then just press C-c C-c to
send the article as you would do normally. The previous article will be
canceled/superseded.

Just remember, kids: There is no 'c' in 'supersede'.

--------------

<<Delayed-Articles>>

Next: [[#Marking-Articles][Marking Articles]], Previous:
[[#Reply-Followup-and-Post][Reply, Followup and Post]], Up:
[[#Summary-Buffer][Summary Buffer]]  
[[[#SEC_Contents][Contents]]][[[#Index][Index]]]

*** 4.6 Delayed Articles [[#Delayed-Articles-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Delayed-Articles-1
:CLASS: section
:END:
Sometimes, you might wish to delay the sending of a message. For
example, you might wish to arrange for a message to turn up just in time
to remind your about the birthday of your Significant Other. For this,
there is the =gnus-delay= package. Setup is simple:

#+begin_src lisp-preformatted
(gnus-delay-initialize)
#+end_src

Normally, to send a message you use the C-c C-c command from Message
mode. To delay a message, use C-c C-j (=gnus-delay-article=) instead.
This will ask you for how long the message should be delayed. Possible
answers are:

- A time span. Consists of an integer and a letter. For example, =42d=
  means to delay for 42 days. Available letters are =m= (minutes), =h=
  (hours), =d= (days), =w= (weeks), =M= (months) and =Y= (years).
- A specific date. Looks like =YYYY-MM-DD=. The message will be delayed
  until that day, at a specific time (eight o'clock by default). See
  also =gnus-delay-default-hour=.
- A specific time of day. Given in =hh:mm= format, 24h, no am/pm stuff.
  The deadline will be at that time today, except if that time has
  already passed, then it's at the given time tomorrow. So if it's ten
  o'clock in the morning and you specify =11:15=, then the deadline is
  one hour and fifteen minutes hence. But if you specify =9:20=, that
  means a time tomorrow.

The action of the =gnus-delay-article= command is influenced by a couple
of variables:

- <<index-gnus_002ddelay_002ddefault_002dhour>>=gnus-delay-default-hour=
  [[#index-gnus_002ddelay_002ddefault_002dhour][¶]] :: When you specify
  a specific date, the message will be due on that hour on the given
  date. Possible values are integers 0 through 23.

- <<index-gnus_002ddelay_002ddefault_002ddelay>>=gnus-delay-default-delay=
  [[#index-gnus_002ddelay_002ddefault_002ddelay][¶]] :: This is a string
  and gives the default delay. It can be of any of the formats described
  above.

- <<index-gnus_002ddelay_002dgroup>>=gnus-delay-group=
  [[#index-gnus_002ddelay_002dgroup][¶]] :: Delayed articles will be
  kept in this group on the drafts server until they are due. You
  probably don't need to change this. The default value is ="delayed"=.

- <<index-gnus_002ddelay_002dheader>>=gnus-delay-header=
  [[#index-gnus_002ddelay_002dheader][¶]] :: The deadline for each
  article will be stored in a header. This variable is a string and
  gives the header name. You probably don't need to change this. The
  default value is ="X-Gnus-Delayed"=.

The way delaying works is like this: when you use the
=gnus-delay-article= command, you give a certain delay. Gnus calculates
the deadline of the message and stores it in the =X-Gnus-Delayed= header
and puts the message in the =nndraft:delayed= group.

And whenever you get new news, Gnus looks through the group for articles
which are due and sends them. It uses the =gnus-delay-send-queue=
function for this. By default, this function is added to the hook
=gnus-get-new-news-hook=. But of course, you can change this. Maybe you
want to use the demon to send drafts? Just tell the demon to execute the
=gnus-delay-send-queue= function.

- <<index-gnus_002ddelay_002dinitialize>>=gnus-delay-initialize=
  [[#index-gnus_002ddelay_002dinitialize][¶]] :: By default, this
  function installs =gnus-delay-send-queue= in =gnus-get-new-news-hook=.
  But it accepts the optional second argument =no-check=. If it is
  non-=nil=, =gnus-get-new-news-hook= is not changed. The optional first
  argument is ignored.

  For example, =(gnus-delay-initialize nil t)= means to do nothing.
  Presumably, you want to use the demon for sending due delayed
  articles. Just don't forget to set that up :-)

--------------

*** 4.7 Marking Articles [[#Marking-Articles-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Marking-Articles-1
:CLASS: section
:END:
There are several marks you can set on an article.

You have marks that decide the /readedness/ (whoo, neato-keano neologism
ohoy!) of the article. Alphabetic marks generally mean /read/, while
non-alphabetic characters generally mean /unread/.

In addition, you also have marks that do not affect readedness.

- [[#Unread-Articles][Unread Articles]]
- [[#Read-Articles][Read Articles]]
- [[#Other-Marks][Other Marks]]
- [[#Setting-Marks][Setting Marks]]
- [[#Generic-Marking-Commands][Generic Marking Commands]]
- [[#Setting-Process-Marks][Setting Process Marks]]

--------------

<<Unread-Articles>>

Next: [[#Read-Articles][Read Articles]], Up:
[[#Marking-Articles][Marking Articles]]  
[[[#SEC_Contents][Contents]]][[[#Index][Index]]]

**** 4.7.1 Unread Articles [[#Unread-Articles-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Unread-Articles-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
The following marks mark articles as (kinda) unread, in one form or
other.

- <<index-gnus_002dticked_002dmark>>‘=!='
  [[#index-gnus_002dticked_002dmark][¶]] :: Marked as ticked
  (=gnus-ticked-mark=).

  /Ticked articles/ are articles that will remain visible always. If you
  see an article that you find interesting, or you want to put off
  reading it, or replying to it, until sometime later, you'd typically
  tick it. However, articles can be expired (from news servers by the
  news server software, Gnus itself never expires ticked messages), so
  if you want to keep an article forever, you'll have to make it
  persistent (see [[#Persistent-Articles][Persistent Articles]]).

- <<index-gnus_002ddormant_002dmark>>‘=?='
  [[#index-gnus_002ddormant_002dmark][¶]] :: Marked as dormant
  (=gnus-dormant-mark=).

  /Dormant articles/ will only appear in the summary buffer if there are
  followups to it. If you want to see them even if they don't have
  followups, you can use the / D command (see [[#Limiting][Limiting]]).
  Otherwise (except for the visibility issue), they are just like ticked
  messages.

- <<index-gnus_002dunread_002dmark-1>>‘=SPC='
  [[#index-gnus_002dunread_002dmark-1][¶]] :: Marked as unread
  (=gnus-unread-mark=).

  /Unread articles/ are articles that haven't been read at all yet.

--------------

<<Read-Articles>>

Next: [[#Other-Marks][Other Marks]], Previous:
[[#Unread-Articles][Unread Articles]], Up:
[[#Marking-Articles][Marking Articles]]  
[[[#SEC_Contents][Contents]]][[[#Index][Index]]]

**** 4.7.2 Read Articles [[#Read-Articles-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Read-Articles-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
All the following marks mark articles as read.

- <<index-gnus_002ddel_002dmark>>‘=r='
  [[#index-gnus_002ddel_002dmark][¶]] :: These are articles that the
  user has marked as read with the d command manually, more or less
  (=gnus-del-mark=).

- <<index-gnus_002dread_002dmark>>‘=R='
  [[#index-gnus_002dread_002dmark][¶]] :: Articles that have actually
  been read (=gnus-read-mark=).

- <<index-gnus_002dancient_002dmark>>‘=O='
  [[#index-gnus_002dancient_002dmark][¶]] :: Articles that were marked
  as read in previous sessions and are now /old/ (=gnus-ancient-mark=).

- <<index-gnus_002dkilled_002dmark>>‘=K='
  [[#index-gnus_002dkilled_002dmark][¶]] :: Marked as killed
  (=gnus-killed-mark=).

- <<index-gnus_002dkill_002dfile_002dmark>>‘=X='
  [[#index-gnus_002dkill_002dfile_002dmark][¶]] :: Marked as killed by
  kill files (=gnus-kill-file-mark=).

- <<index-gnus_002dlow_002dscore_002dmark>>‘=Y='
  [[#index-gnus_002dlow_002dscore_002dmark][¶]] :: Marked as read by
  having too low a score (=gnus-low-score-mark=).

- <<index-gnus_002dcatchup_002dmark>>‘=C='
  [[#index-gnus_002dcatchup_002dmark][¶]] :: Marked as read by a catchup
  (=gnus-catchup-mark=).

- <<index-gnus_002dcanceled_002dmark>>‘=G='
  [[#index-gnus_002dcanceled_002dmark][¶]] :: Canceled article
  (=gnus-canceled-mark=)

- <<index-gnus_002dsparse_002dmark>>‘=Q='
  [[#index-gnus_002dsparse_002dmark][¶]] :: Sparsely reffed article
  (=gnus-sparse-mark=). See
  [[#Customizing-Threading][Customizing Threading]].

- <<index-gnus_002dduplicate_002dmark>>‘=M='
  [[#index-gnus_002dduplicate_002dmark][¶]] :: Article marked as read by
  duplicate suppression (=gnus-duplicate-mark=). See
  [[#Duplicate-Suppression][Duplicate Suppression]].

All these marks just mean that the article is marked as read, really.
They are interpreted differently when doing adaptive scoring, though.

One more special mark, though:

- <<index-gnus_002dexpirable_002dmark>>‘=E='
  [[#index-gnus_002dexpirable_002dmark][¶]] :: Marked as expirable
  (=gnus-expirable-mark=).

  Marking articles as /expirable/ (or have them marked as such
  automatically) doesn't make much sense in normal groups---a user
  doesn't control expiring of news articles, but in mail groups, for
  instance, articles marked as /expirable/ can be deleted by Gnus at any
  time.

--------------

<<Other-Marks>>

[[#Read-Articles][Read Articles]], Up:
[[#Marking-Articles][Marking Articles]]  
[[[#SEC_Contents][Contents]]][[[#Index][Index]]]

**** 4.7.3 Other Marks [[#Other-Marks-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Other-Marks-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
There are some marks that have nothing to do with whether the article is
read or not.

- You can set a bookmark in the current article. Say you are reading a
  long thesis on cats' urinary tracts, and have to go home for dinner
  before you've finished reading the thesis. You can then set a bookmark
  in the article, and Gnus will jump to this bookmark the next time it
  encounters the article. See [[#Setting-Marks][Setting Marks]].
-  All articles that you have replied to or made a followup to (i.e.,
  have answered) will be marked with an ‘=A=' in the second column
  (=gnus-replied-mark=).
-  All articles that you have forwarded will be marked with an ‘=F=' in
  the second column (=gnus-forwarded-mark=).
-  Articles stored in the article cache will be marked with an ‘=*=' in
  the second column (=gnus-cached-mark=). See
  [[#Article-Caching][Article Caching]].
-  Articles “saved” (in some manner or other; not necessarily
  religiously) are marked with an ‘=S=' in the second column
  (=gnus-saved-mark=).
-  Articles that haven't been seen before in Gnus by the user are marked
  with a ‘=.=' in the second column (=gnus-unseen-mark=).
-  When using the Gnus agent (see [[#Agent-Basics][Agent Basics]]),
  articles may be downloaded for unplugged (offline) viewing. If you are
  using the ‘=%O=' spec, these articles get the ‘=+=' mark in that spec.
  (The variable =gnus-downloaded-mark= controls which character to use.)
-  When using the Gnus agent (see [[#Agent-Basics][Agent Basics]]), some
  articles might not have been downloaded. Such articles cannot be
  viewed while you are unplugged (offline). If you are using the ‘=%O='
  spec, these articles get the ‘=-=' mark in that spec. (The variable
  =gnus-undownloaded-mark= controls which character to use.)
-  The Gnus agent (see [[#Agent-Basics][Agent Basics]]) downloads some
  articles automatically, but it is also possible to explicitly mark
  articles for download, even if they would not be downloaded
  automatically. Such explicitly-marked articles get the ‘=%=' mark in
  the first column. (The variable =gnus-downloadable-mark= controls
  which character to use.)
-  If the ‘=%e=' spec is used, the presence of threads or not will be
  marked with =gnus-not-empty-thread-mark= and =gnus-empty-thread-mark=
  in the third column, respectively.
-  Finally we have the /process mark/ (=gnus-process-mark=). A variety
  of commands react to the presence of the process mark. For instance, X
  u (=gnus-uu-decode-uu=) will uudecode and view all articles that have
  been marked with the process mark. Articles marked with the process
  mark have a ‘=#=' in the second column.

You might have noticed that most of these “non-readedness” marks appear
in the second column by default. So if you have a cached, saved, replied
article that you have process-marked, what will that look like?

Nothing much. The precedence rules go as follows: process -> cache ->
replied -> saved. So if the article is in the cache and is replied,
you'll only see the cache mark and not the replied mark.

--------------

<<Setting-Marks>>

**** 4.7.4 Setting Marks [[#Setting-Marks-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Setting-Marks-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
All the marking commands understand the numeric prefix.

-  <<index-M-c-_0028Summary_0029>>M c
  [[#index-M-c-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  M-u :: Clear all readedness-marks from the current article
  (=gnus-summary-clear-mark-forward=). In other words, mark the article
  as unread.

-  <<index-_0021-_0028Summary_0029>>M t
  [[#index-_0021-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  ! :: Tick the current article (=gnus-summary-tick-article-forward=).
  See [[#Article-Caching][Article Caching]].

-  <<index-_003f-_0028Summary_0029>>M ?
  [[#index-_003f-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  ? :: Mark the current article as dormant
  (=gnus-summary-mark-as-dormant=). See
  [[#Article-Caching][Article Caching]].

-  <<index-M-d-_0028Summary_0029>>M d
  [[#index-M-d-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  d :: Mark the current article as read
  (=gnus-summary-mark-as-read-forward=).

-  <<index-D-_0028Summary_0029>>D
  [[#index-D-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark the current article as read
  and move point to the previous line
  (=gnus-summary-mark-as-read-backward=).

-  <<index-k-_0028Summary_0029>>M k [[#index-k-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  k :: Mark all articles that have the same subject as the current one
  as read, and then select the next unread article
  (=gnus-summary-kill-same-subject-and-select=).

-  <<index-M-K-_0028Summary_0029>>M K
  [[#index-M-K-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  C-k :: Mark all articles that have the same subject as the current one
  as read (=gnus-summary-kill-same-subject=).

-  <<index-M-C-_0028Summary_0029>>M C
  [[#index-M-C-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all unread articles as
  read (=gnus-summary-catchup=).

-  <<index-M-C_002dc-_0028Summary_0029>>M C-c
  [[#index-M-C_002dc-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all articles in the
  group as read---even the ticked and dormant articles
  (=gnus-summary-catchup-all=).

-  <<index-M-H-_0028Summary_0029>>M H
  [[#index-M-H-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Catchup the current group to
  point (before the point) (=gnus-summary-catchup-to-here=).

-  <<index-M-h-_0028Summary_0029>>M h
  [[#index-M-h-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Catchup the current group from
  point (after the point) (=gnus-summary-catchup-from-here=).

-  <<index-C_002dw-_0028Summary_0029>>C-w
  [[#index-C_002dw-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all articles between
  point and mark as read (=gnus-summary-mark-region-as-read=).

-  <<index-M-V-k-_0028Summary_0029>>M V k
  [[#index-M-V-k-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Kill all articles with scores
  below the default score (or below the numeric prefix)
  (=gnus-summary-kill-below=).

-  <<index-M-e-_0028Summary_0029>>M e
  [[#index-M-e-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  E :: Mark the current article as expirable
  (=gnus-summary-mark-as-expirable=).

-  <<index-M-b-_0028Summary_0029>>M b
  [[#index-M-b-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Set a bookmark in the current
  article (=gnus-summary-set-bookmark=).

-  <<index-M-B-_0028Summary_0029>>M B
  [[#index-M-B-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Remove the bookmark from the
  current article (=gnus-summary-remove-bookmark=).

-  <<index-M-V-c-_0028Summary_0029>>M V c
  [[#index-M-V-c-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Clear all marks from articles
  with scores over the default score (or over the numeric prefix)
  (=gnus-summary-clear-above=).

-  <<index-M-V-u-_0028Summary_0029>>M V u
  [[#index-M-V-u-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Tick all articles with scores
  over the default score (or over the numeric prefix)
  (=gnus-summary-tick-above=).

-  <<index-M-V-m-_0028Summary_0029>>M V m
  [[#index-M-V-m-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Prompt for a mark, and mark
  all articles with scores over the default score (or over the numeric
  prefix) with this mark (=gnus-summary-clear-above=).

The =gnus-summary-goto-unread= variable controls what action should be
taken after setting a mark. If non-=nil=, point will move to the
next/previous unread article. If =nil=, point will just move one line up
or down. As a special case, if this variable is =never=, all the marking
commands as well as other commands (like SPC) will move to the next
article, whether it is unread or not. The default is =t=.

--------------

<<Generic-Marking-Commands>>

Next: [[#Setting-Process-Marks][Setting Process Marks]], Previous:
[[#Setting-Marks][Setting Marks]], Up:
[[#Marking-Articles][Marking Articles]]

**** 4.7.5 Generic Marking Commands [[#Generic-Marking-Commands-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Generic-Marking-Commands-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
Some people would like the command that ticks an article (!) to go to
the next article. Others would like it to go to the next unread article.
Yet others would like it to stay on the current article. And even though
I haven't heard of anybody wanting it to go to the previous (unread)
article, I'm sure there are people that want that as well.

Multiply these five behaviors with five different marking commands, and
you get a potentially complex set of variable to control what each
command should do.

To sidestep that mess, Gnus provides commands that do all these
different things. They can be found on the M M map in the summary
buffer. Type M M C-h to see them all---there are too many of them to
list in this manual.

While you can use these commands directly, most users would prefer
altering the summary mode keymap. For instance, if you would like the !
command to go to the next article instead of the next unread article,
you could say something like:

#+begin_src lisp-preformatted
(add-hook 'gnus-summary-mode-hook 'my-alter-summary-map)
(defun my-alter-summary-map ()
  (keymap-local-set "!" 'gnus-summary-put-mark-as-ticked-next))
#+end_src

or

#+begin_src lisp-preformatted
(defun my-alter-summary-map ()
  (keymap-local-set "!" "MM!n"))
#+end_src

--------------

<<Setting-Process-Marks>>

Previous: [[#Generic-Marking-Commands][Generic Marking Commands]], Up:
[[#Marking-Articles][Marking Articles]]  
[[[#SEC_Contents][Contents]]][[[#Index][Index]]]

**** 4.7.6 Setting Process Marks [[#Setting-Process-Marks-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Setting-Process-Marks-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
Process marks are displayed as =#= in the summary buffer, and are used
for marking articles in such a way that other commands will process
these articles. For instance, if you process mark four articles and then
use the * command, Gnus will enter these four articles into the cache.
For more information, see [[#Process_002fPrefix][Process/Prefix]].

-  <<index-_0023-_0028Summary_0029>>M P p
  [[#index-_0023-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  ​# :: Toggle the process mark for the current article
  (=gnus-summary-mark-as-processable=).\\
  If =gnus-process-mark-toggle= is =nil=, set the process mark for the
  current article.

-  <<index-M-P-u-_0028Summary_0029>>M P u
  [[#index-M-P-u-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  M-# :: Remove the process mark, if any, from the current article
  (=gnus-summary-unmark-as-processable=).

-  <<index-M-P-U-_0028Summary_0029>>M P U
  [[#index-M-P-U-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Remove the process mark from
  all articles (=gnus-summary-unmark-all-processable=).

-  <<index-M-P-i-_0028Summary_0029>>M P i
  [[#index-M-P-i-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Invert the list of process
  marked articles (=gnus-uu-invert-processable=).

-  <<index-M-P-R-_0028Summary_0029>>M P R
  [[#index-M-P-R-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark articles that have a
  =Subject= header that matches a regular expression
  (=gnus-uu-mark-by-regexp=).

-  <<index-M-P-G-_0028Summary_0029>>M P G
  [[#index-M-P-G-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Unmark articles that have a
  =Subject= header that matches a regular expression
  (=gnus-uu-unmark-by-regexp=).

-  <<index-M-P-r-_0028Summary_0029>>M P r
  [[#index-M-P-r-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark articles in region
  (=gnus-uu-mark-region=).

-  <<index-M-P-g-_0028Summary_0029>>M P g
  [[#index-M-P-g-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Unmark articles in region
  (=gnus-uu-unmark-region=).

-  <<index-M-P-t-_0028Summary_0029>>M P t
  [[#index-M-P-t-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all articles in the
  current (sub)thread (=gnus-uu-mark-thread=).

-  <<index-M-P-T-_0028Summary_0029>>M P T
  [[#index-M-P-T-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Unmark all articles in the
  current (sub)thread (=gnus-uu-unmark-thread=).

-  <<index-M-P-v-_0028Summary_0029>>M P v
  [[#index-M-P-v-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all articles that have a
  score above the prefix argument (=gnus-uu-mark-over=).

-  <<index-M-P-s-_0028Summary_0029>>M P s
  [[#index-M-P-s-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all articles in the
  current series (=gnus-uu-mark-series=).

-  <<index-M-P-S-_0028Summary_0029>>M P S
  [[#index-M-P-S-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all series that have
  already had some articles marked (=gnus-uu-mark-sparse=).

-  <<index-M-P-a-_0028Summary_0029>>M P a
  [[#index-M-P-a-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all articles in series
  order (=gnus-uu-mark-all=).

-  <<index-M-P-b-_0028Summary_0029>>M P b
  [[#index-M-P-b-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all articles in the
  buffer in the order they appear (=gnus-uu-mark-buffer=).

-  <<index-M-P-k-_0028Summary_0029>>M P k
  [[#index-M-P-k-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Push the current process mark
  set onto the stack and unmark all articles
  (=gnus-summary-kill-process-mark=).

-  <<index-M-P-y-_0028Summary_0029>>M P y
  [[#index-M-P-y-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Pop the previous process mark
  set from the stack and restore it (=gnus-summary-yank-process-mark=).

-  <<index-M-P-w-_0028Summary_0029>>M P w
  [[#index-M-P-w-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Push the current process mark
  set onto the stack (=gnus-summary-save-process-mark=).

Also see the & command in
[[#Searching-for-Articles][Searching for Articles]], for how to set
process marks based on article body contents.

--------------

*** 4.8 Limiting [[#Limiting-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Limiting-1
:CLASS: section
:END:
It can be convenient to limit the summary buffer to just show some
subset of the articles currently in the group. The effect most limit
commands have is to remove a few (or many) articles from the summary
buffer.

Limiting commands work on subsets of the articles already fetched from
the servers. These commands don't query the server for additional
articles.

-  <<index-_002f-_002f-_0028Summary_0029>>/ /
  [[#index-_002f-_002f-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  / s :: Limit the summary buffer to articles that match some subject
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-subject=). If given a prefix, exclude matching
  articles.

-  <<index-_002f-a-_0028Summary_0029>>/ a
  [[#index-_002f-a-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  articles that match some author (=gnus-summary-limit-to-author=). If
  given a prefix, exclude matching articles.

-  <<index-_002f-R-_0028Summary_0029>>/ R
  [[#index-_002f-R-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  articles that match some recipient
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-recipient=). If given a prefix, exclude
  matching articles.

-  <<index-_002f-A-_0028Summary_0029>>/ A
  [[#index-_002f-A-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  articles in which contents of From, To or Cc header match a given
  address (=gnus-summary-limit-to-address=). If given a prefix, exclude
  matching articles.

-  <<index-_002f-S-_0028Summary_0029>>/ S
  [[#index-_002f-S-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  articles that aren't part of any displayed threads
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-singletons=). If given a prefix, limit to
  articles that are part of displayed threads.

-  <<index-_002f-x-_0028Summary_0029>>/ x
  [[#index-_002f-x-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  articles that match one of the “extra” headers (see
  [[#To-From-Newsgroups][To From Newsgroups]])
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-extra=). If given a prefix, exclude matching
  articles.

-  <<index-_002f-u-_0028Summary_0029>>/ u
  [[#index-_002f-u-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  x :: Limit the summary buffer to articles not marked as read
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-unread=). If given a prefix, limit the buffer
  to articles strictly unread. This means that ticked and dormant
  articles will also be excluded.

-  <<index-_002f-m-_0028Summary_0029>>/ m
  [[#index-_002f-m-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Ask for a mark and then
  limit to all articles that have been marked with that mark
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-marks=).

-  <<index-_002f-t-_0028Summary_0029>>/ t
  [[#index-_002f-t-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Ask for a number and then
  limit the summary buffer to articles older than (or equal to) that
  number of days (=gnus-summary-limit-to-age=). If given a prefix, limit
  to articles younger than that number of days.

-  <<index-_002f-n-_0028Summary_0029>>/ n
  [[#index-_002f-n-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: With prefix ‘=n=', limit
  the summary buffer to the next ‘=n=' articles. If not given a prefix,
  use the process marked articles instead.
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-articles=).

-  <<index-_002f-w-_0028Summary_0029>>/ w
  [[#index-_002f-w-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Pop the previous limit off
  the stack and restore it (=gnus-summary-pop-limit=). If given a
  prefix, pop all limits off the stack.

-  <<index-_002f-_002e-_0028Summary_0029>>/ .
  [[#index-_002f-_002e-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary
  buffer to the unseen articles (=gnus-summary-limit-to-unseen=).

-  <<index-_002f-v-_0028Summary_0029>>/ v
  [[#index-_002f-v-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  articles that have a score at or above some score
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-score=). If given a prefix, below some score.

-  <<index-_002f-p-_0028Summary_0029>>/ p
  [[#index-_002f-p-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  articles that satisfy the =display= group parameter predicate
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-display-predicate=). See
  [[#Group-Parameters][Group Parameters]], for more on this predicate.

-  <<index-_002f-r-_0028Summary_0029>>/ r
  [[#index-_002f-r-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  replied articles (=gnus-summary-limit-to-replied=). If given a prefix,
  exclude replied articles.

-  <<index-M-S-_0028Summary_0029>>/ E
  [[#index-M-S-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  M S :: Include all expunged articles in the limit
  (=gnus-summary-limit-include-expunged=).

-  <<index-_002f-D-_0028Summary_0029>>/ D
  [[#index-_002f-D-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Include all dormant
  articles in the limit (=gnus-summary-limit-include-dormant=).

-  <<index-_002f-_002a-_0028Summary_0029>>/ *
  [[#index-_002f-_002a-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Include all cached
  articles in the limit (=gnus-summary-limit-include-cached=).

-  <<index-_002f-d-_0028Summary_0029>>/ d
  [[#index-_002f-d-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Exclude all dormant
  articles from the limit (=gnus-summary-limit-exclude-dormant=).

-  <<index-_002f-M-_0028Summary_0029>>/ M
  [[#index-_002f-M-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Exclude all marked articles
  (=gnus-summary-limit-exclude-marks=).

-  <<index-_002f-T-_0028Summary_0029>>/ T
  [[#index-_002f-T-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Include all the articles in
  the current thread in the limit.

-  <<index-_002f-c-_0028Summary_0029>>/ c
  [[#index-_002f-c-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Exclude all dormant
  articles that have no children from the limit\\
  (=gnus-summary-limit-exclude-childless-dormant=).

-  <<index-_002f-C-_0028Summary_0029>>/ C
  [[#index-_002f-C-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Mark all excluded unread
  articles as read (=gnus-summary-limit-mark-excluded-as-read=). If
  given a prefix, also mark excluded ticked and dormant articles as
  read.

-  <<index-_002f-b-_0028Summary_0029>>/ b
  [[#index-_002f-b-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Limit the summary buffer to
  articles that have bodies that match a certain regexp
  (=gnus-summary-limit-to-bodies=). If given a prefix, reverse the
  limit. This command is quite slow since it requires selecting each
  article to find the matches.

-  <<index-_002f-h-_0028Summary_0029>>/ h
  [[#index-_002f-h-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Like the previous command,
  only limit to headers instead (=gnus-summary-limit-to-headers=).

The following commands aren't limiting commands, but use the / prefix as
well.

-  <<index-_002f-N-_0028Summary_0029>>/ N
  [[#index-_002f-N-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Insert all new articles in
  the summary buffer. It scans for new emails if
  =back-end==-get-new-mail= is non-=nil=.

-  <<index-_002f-o-_0028Summary_0029>>/ o
  [[#index-_002f-o-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Insert all old articles in
  the summary buffer. If given a numbered prefix, fetch this number of
  articles.

*** 4.9 Threading [[#Threading-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Threading-1
:CLASS: section
:END:
Gnus threads articles by default. /To thread/ is to put responses to
articles directly after the articles they respond to---in a hierarchical
fashion.

Threading is done by looking at the =References= headers of the
articles. In a perfect world, this would be enough to build pretty
trees, but unfortunately, the =References= header is often broken or
simply missing. Weird news propagation exacerbates the problem, so one
has to employ other heuristics to get pleasing results. A plethora of
approaches exists, as detailed in horrible detail in
[[#Customizing-Threading][Customizing Threading]].

First, a quick overview of the concepts:

- /root/ :: The top-most article in a thread; the first article in the
  thread.

- /thread/ :: A tree-like article structure.

- /sub-thread/ :: A small(er) section of this tree-like structure.

- /loose threads/ :: Threads often lose their roots due to article
  expiry, or due to the root already having been read in a previous
  session, and not displayed in the summary buffer. We then typically
  have many sub-threads that really belong to one thread, but are
  without connecting roots. These are called loose threads.

- /thread gathering/ :: An attempt to gather loose threads into bigger
  threads.

- /sparse threads/ :: A thread where the missing articles have been
  “guessed” at, and are displayed as empty lines in the summary buffer.

- [[#Customizing-Threading][Customizing Threading]]
- [[#Thread-Commands][Thread Commands]]

--------------

**** 4.9.1.1 Loose Threads [[#Loose-Threads-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Loose-Threads-1
:CLASS: subsubsection
:END:
- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dmake_002dfalse_002droot>>=gnus-summary-make-false-root=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dmake_002dfalse_002droot][¶]] :: If
  non-=nil=, Gnus will gather all loose subtrees into one big tree and
  create a dummy root at the top. (Wait a minute. Root at the top? Yup.)
  Loose subtrees occur when the real root has expired, or you've read or
  killed the root in a previous session.

  When there is no real root of a thread, Gnus will have to fudge
  something. This variable says what fudging method Gnus should use.
  There are four possible values:

  - =adopt= :: Gnus will make the first of the orphaned articles the
    parent. This parent will adopt all the other articles. The adopted
    articles will be marked as such by pointy brackets (‘=<>=') instead
    of the standard square brackets (‘=[]='). This is the default
    method.

  -  <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002ddummy_002dline_002dformat>>=dummy=
    [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002ddummy_002dline_002dformat][¶]] :: Gnus
    will create a dummy summary line that will pretend to be the parent.
    This dummy line does not correspond to any real article, so
    selecting it will just select the first real article after the dummy
    article. =gnus-summary-dummy-line-format= is used to specify the
    format of the dummy roots. It accepts only one format spec: ‘=S=',
    which is the subject of the article. See
    [[#Formatting-Variables][Formatting Variables]]. If you want all
    threads to have a dummy root, even the non-gathered ones, set
    =gnus-summary-make-false-root-always= to =t=.

  - =empty= :: Gnus won't actually make any article the parent, but
    simply leave the subject field of all orphans except the first
    empty. (Actually, it will use =gnus-summary-same-subject= as the
    subject (see [[#Summary-Buffer-Format][Summary Buffer Format]]).)

  - =none= :: Don't make any article parent at all. Just gather the
    threads and display them after one another.

  - =nil= :: Don't gather loose threads.

- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dgather_002dsubject_002dlimit>>=gnus-summary-gather-subject-limit=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dgather_002dsubject_002dlimit][¶]] :: Loose
  threads are gathered by comparing subjects of articles. If this
  variable is =nil=, Gnus requires an exact match between the subjects
  of the loose threads before gathering them into one big super-thread.
  This might be too strict a requirement, what with the presence of
  stupid newsreaders that chop off long subject lines. If you think so,
  set this variable to, say, 20 to require that only the first 20
  characters of the subjects have to match. If you set this variable to
  a really low number, you'll find that Gnus will gather everything in
  sight into one thread, which isn't very helpful.

  If you set this variable to the special value =fuzzy=, Gnus will use a
  fuzzy string comparison algorithm on the subjects (see
  [[#Fuzzy-Matching][Fuzzy Matching]]).

- <<index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dsubject_002dfuzzy_002dregexp>>=gnus-simplify-subject-fuzzy-regexp=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dsubject_002dfuzzy_002dregexp][¶]] :: This
  can either be a regular expression or list of regular expressions that
  match strings that will be removed from subjects if fuzzy subject
  simplification is used.

- <<index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dignored_002dprefixes>>=gnus-simplify-ignored-prefixes=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dignored_002dprefixes][¶]] :: If you set
  =gnus-summary-gather-subject-limit= to something as low as 10, you
  might consider setting this variable to something sensible:

  #+begin_src lisp-preformatted
  (setq gnus-simplify-ignored-prefixes
        (concat
         "\\`\\[?\\("
         (regexp-opt '("looking"
                       "wanted" "followup" "summary" "summary of"
                       "help" "query" "problem" "question"
                       "answer" "reference" "announce"
                       "How can I" "How to" "Comparison of"
                       ;; ...
                       ))
         "\\)\\s *\\("
         (regexp-opt '("for" "for reference" "with" "about"))
         "\\)?\\]?:?[ \t]*"))
  #+end_src

  All words that match this regexp will be removed before comparing two
  subjects.

- <<index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dsubject_002dfunctions>>=gnus-simplify-subject-functions=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dsubject_002dfunctions][¶]] :: If
  non-=nil=, this variable overrides
  =gnus-summary-gather-subject-limit=. This variable should be a list of
  functions to apply to the =Subject= string iteratively to arrive at
  the simplified version of the string.

  Useful functions to put in this list include:

  - <<index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dsubject_002dre>>=gnus-simplify-subject-re=
    [[#index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dsubject_002dre][¶]] :: Strip the
    leading ‘=Re:='.

  - <<index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dsubject_002dfuzzy>>=gnus-simplify-subject-fuzzy=
    [[#index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dsubject_002dfuzzy][¶]] :: Simplify
    fuzzily.

  - <<index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dwhitespace>>=gnus-simplify-whitespace=
    [[#index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dwhitespace][¶]] :: Remove excessive
    whitespace.

  - <<index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dall_002dwhitespace>>=gnus-simplify-all-whitespace=
    [[#index-gnus_002dsimplify_002dall_002dwhitespace][¶]] :: Remove all
    whitespace.

  You may also write your own functions, of course.

- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dgather_002dexclude_002dsubject>>=gnus-summary-gather-exclude-subject=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dgather_002dexclude_002dsubject][¶]] :: Since
  loose thread gathering is done on subjects only, that might lead to
  many false hits, especially with certain common subjects like and
  ‘=(none)='. To make the situation slightly better, you can use the
  regexp =gnus-summary-gather-exclude-subject= to say what subjects
  should be excluded from the gathering process.\\
  The default is ‘=^ *$\\|^(none)$='.

- <<index-gnus_002dsummary_002dthread_002dgathering_002dfunction>>=gnus-summary-thread-gathering-function=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsummary_002dthread_002dgathering_002dfunction][¶]] :: Gnus
  gathers threads by looking at =Subject= headers. This means that
  totally unrelated articles may end up in the same “thread”, which is
  confusing. An alternate approach is to look at all the =Message-ID=s
  in all the =References= headers to find matches. This will ensure that
  no gathered threads ever include unrelated articles, but it also means
  that people who have posted with broken newsreaders won't be gathered
  properly. The choice is yours---plague or cholera:

  - <<index-gnus_002dgather_002dthreads_002dby_002dsubject>>=gnus-gather-threads-by-subject=
    [[#index-gnus_002dgather_002dthreads_002dby_002dsubject][¶]] :: This
    function is the default gathering function and looks at =Subject=s
    exclusively.

  - <<index-gnus_002dgather_002dthreads_002dby_002dreferences>>=gnus-gather-threads-by-references=
    [[#index-gnus_002dgather_002dthreads_002dby_002dreferences][¶]] :: This
    function looks at =References= headers exclusively.

  If you want to test gathering by =References=, you could say something
  like:

  #+begin_src lisp-preformatted
  (setq gnus-summary-thread-gathering-function
        'gnus-gather-threads-by-references)
  #+end_src

--------------

**** 4.9.1.2 Filling In Threads [[#Filling-In-Threads-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Filling-In-Threads-1
:CLASS: subsubsection
:END:
- <<index-gnus_002dfetch_002dold_002dheaders>>=gnus-fetch-old-headers=
  [[#index-gnus_002dfetch_002dold_002dheaders][¶]] :: If non-=nil=, Gnus
  will attempt to build old threads by fetching more old
  headers---headers to articles marked as read. If you would like to
  display as few summary lines as possible, but still connect as many
  loose threads as possible, you should set this variable to =some= or a
  number. If you set it to a number, no more than that number of extra
  old headers will be fetched. In either case, fetching old headers only
  works if the back end you are using carries overview files---this
  would normally be =nntp=, =nnspool=, =nnml=, and =nnmaildir=. Also
  remember that if the root of the thread has been expired by the
  server, there's not much Gnus can do about that.

  This variable can also be set to =invisible=. This won't have any
  visible effects, but is useful if you use the A T command a lot (see
  [[#Finding-the-Parent][Finding the Parent]]).

  The server has to support NOV for any of this to work.

  This feature can seriously impact performance it ignores all locally
  cached header entries. Setting it to =t= for groups for a server that
  doesn't expire articles (such as news.gmane.io), leads to very slow
  summary generation.

- <<index-gnus_002dfetch_002dold_002dephemeral_002dheaders>>=gnus-fetch-old-ephemeral-headers=
  [[#index-gnus_002dfetch_002dold_002dephemeral_002dheaders][¶]] :: Same
  as =gnus-fetch-old-headers=, but only used for ephemeral newsgroups.

- <<index-gnus_002dbuild_002dsparse_002dthreads>>=gnus-build-sparse-threads=
  [[#index-gnus_002dbuild_002dsparse_002dthreads][¶]] :: Fetching old
  headers can be slow. A low-rent similar effect can be gotten by
  setting this variable to =some=. Gnus will then look at the complete
  =References= headers of all articles and try to string together
  articles that belong in the same thread. This will leave /gaps/ in the
  threading display where Gnus guesses that an article is missing from
  the thread. (These gaps appear like normal summary lines. If you
  select a gap, Gnus will try to fetch the article in question.) If this
  variable is =t=, Gnus will display all these “gaps” without regard for
  whether they are useful for completing the thread or not. Finally, if
  this variable is =more=, Gnus won't cut off sparse leaf nodes that
  don't lead anywhere. This variable is =nil= by default.

- <<index-gnus_002dread_002dall_002davailable_002dheaders>>=gnus-read-all-available-headers=
  [[#index-gnus_002dread_002dall_002davailable_002dheaders][¶]] :: This
  is a rather obscure variable that few will find useful. It's intended
  for those non-news newsgroups where the back end has to fetch quite a
  lot to present the summary buffer, and where it's impossible to go
  back to parents of articles. This is mostly the case in the web-based
  groups.

  If you don't use those, then it's safe to leave this as the default
  =nil=. If you want to use this variable, it should be a regexp that
  matches the group name, or =t= for all groups.

--------------

<<More-Threading>>

Next: [[#Low_002dLevel-Threading][Low-Level Threading]], Previous:
[[#Filling-In-Threads][Filling In Threads]], Up:
[[#Customizing-Threading][Customizing Threading]]

**** 4.9.1.3 More Threading [[#More-Threading-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: More-Threading-1
:CLASS: subsubsection
:END:
- <<index-gnus_002dshow_002dthreads>>=gnus-show-threads=
  [[#index-gnus_002dshow_002dthreads][¶]] :: If this variable is =nil=,
  no threading will be done, and all of the rest of the variables here
  will have no effect. Turning threading off will speed group selection
  up a bit, but it is sure to make reading slower and more awkward.

- <<index-gnus_002dthread_002dhide_002dsubtree>>=gnus-thread-hide-subtree=
  [[#index-gnus_002dthread_002dhide_002dsubtree][¶]] :: If non-=nil=,
  all threads will be hidden when the summary buffer is generated.

  This can also be a predicate specifier (see
  [[#Predicate-Specifiers][Predicate Specifiers]]). Available predicates
  are =gnus-article-unread-p= and =gnus-article-unseen-p=.

  Here's an example:

  #+begin_src lisp-preformatted
  (setq gnus-thread-hide-subtree
        '(or gnus-article-unread-p
             gnus-article-unseen-p))
  #+end_src

  (It's a pretty nonsensical example, since all unseen articles are also
  unread, but you get my drift.)

- <<index-gnus_002dthread_002dexpunge_002dbelow>>=gnus-thread-expunge-below=
  [[#index-gnus_002dthread_002dexpunge_002dbelow][¶]] :: All threads
  that have a total score (as defined by =gnus-thread-score-function=)
  less than this number will be expunged. This variable is =nil= by
  default, which means that no threads are expunged.

- <<index-gnus_002dthread_002dhide_002dkilled>>=gnus-thread-hide-killed=
  [[#index-gnus_002dthread_002dhide_002dkilled][¶]] :: if you kill a
  thread and this variable is non-=nil=, the subtree will be hidden.

- <<index-gnus_002dthread_002dignore_002dsubject>>=gnus-thread-ignore-subject=
  [[#index-gnus_002dthread_002dignore_002dsubject][¶]] :: Sometimes
  somebody changes the subject in the middle of a thread. If this
  variable is non-=nil=, which is the default, the subject change is
  ignored. If it is =nil=, a change in the subject will result in a new
  thread.

- <<index-gnus_002dthread_002dindent_002dlevel>>=gnus-thread-indent-level=
  [[#index-gnus_002dthread_002dindent_002dlevel][¶]] :: This is a number
  that says how much each sub-thread should be indented. The default
  is 4.

- <<index-gnus_002dsort_002dgathered_002dthreads_002dfunction>>=gnus-sort-gathered-threads-function=
  [[#index-gnus_002dsort_002dgathered_002dthreads_002dfunction][¶]] :: Sometimes,
  particularly with mailing lists, the order in which mails arrive
  locally is not necessarily the same as the order in which they arrived
  on the mailing list. Consequently, when sorting sub-threads using the
  default =gnus-thread-sort-by-number=, responses can end up appearing
  before the article to which they are responding to. Setting this
  variable to an alternate value (e.g., =gnus-thread-sort-by-date=), in
  a group's parameters or in an appropriate hook (e.g.,
  =gnus-summary-generate-hook=) can produce a more logical sub-thread
  ordering in such instances.

--------------

<<Low_002dLevel-Threading>>

Previous: [[#More-Threading][More Threading]], Up:
[[#Customizing-Threading][Customizing Threading]]

**** 4.9.1.4 Low-Level Threading [[#Low_002dLevel-Threading-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Low_002dLevel-Threading-1
:CLASS: subsubsection
:END:
- <<index-gnus_002dparse_002dheaders_002dhook>>=gnus-parse-headers-hook=
  [[#index-gnus_002dparse_002dheaders_002dhook][¶]] :: Hook run before
  parsing any headers.

- <<index-gnus_002dalter_002dheader_002dfunction>>=gnus-alter-header-function=
  [[#index-gnus_002dalter_002dheader_002dfunction][¶]] :: If non-=nil=,
  this function will be called to allow alteration of article header
  structures. The function is called with one parameter, the article
  header vector, which it may alter in any way. For instance, if you
  have a mail-to-news gateway which alters the =Message-ID=s in
  systematic ways (by adding prefixes and such), you can use this
  variable to un-scramble the =Message-ID=s so that they are more
  meaningful. Here's one example:

  #+begin_src lisp-preformatted
  (setq gnus-alter-header-function 'my-alter-message-id)

  (defun my-alter-message-id (header)
    (let ((id (mail-header-id header)))
      (when (string-match
             "\\(<[^<>@]*\\)\\.?cygnus\\..*@\\([^<>@]*>\\)" id)
        (mail-header-set-id
         (concat (match-string 1 id) "@" (match-string 2 id))
         header))))
  #+end_src

  And another example: the protonmail bridge adds fake message-ids to
  =References= in message headers, which can confuse threading. To
  remove these spurious ids

  #+begin_src lisp-preformatted
  (setq gnus-alter-header-function 'fix-protonmail-references)

  (defun fix-protonmail-references (header)
    (setf (mail-header-references header)
          (mapconcat
           #'(lambda (x) (if (string-search "protonmail.internalid" x) "" x))
           (gnus-split-references (mail-header-references header)) " "))
    header)


  #+end_src

**** 4.9.2 Thread Commands [[#Thread-Commands-1][¶]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: Thread-Commands-1
:CLASS: subsection
:END:
-  <<index-T-k-_0028Summary_0029>>T k
  [[#index-T-k-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  C-M-k :: Mark all articles in the current (sub-)thread as read
  (=gnus-summary-kill-thread=). If the prefix argument is positive,
  remove all marks instead. If the prefix argument is negative, tick
  articles instead.

-  <<index-T-l-_0028Summary_0029>>T l
  [[#index-T-l-_0028Summary_0029][¶]]\\
  C-M-l :: Lower the score of the current (sub-)thread
  (=gnus-summary-lower-thread=).

-  <<index-T-i-_0028Summary_0029>>T i
  [[#index-T-i-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Increase the score of the
  current (sub-)thread (=gnus-summary-raise-thread=).

-  <<index-T-_0023-_0028Summary_0029>>T #
  [[#index-T-_0023-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Set the process mark on the
  current (sub-)thread (=gnus-uu-mark-thread=).

-  <<index-T-M_002d_0023-_0028Summary_0029>>T M-#
  [[#index-T-M_002d_0023-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Remove the process
  mark from the current (sub-)thread (=gnus-uu-unmark-thread=).

-  <<index-T-T-_0028Summary_0029>>T T
  [[#index-T-T-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Toggle threading
  (=gnus-summary-toggle-threads=).

-  <<index-T-s-_0028Summary_0029>>T s
  [[#index-T-s-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Expose the (sub-)thread hidden
  under the current article, if any\\
  (=gnus-summary-show-thread=).

-  <<index-T-h-_0028Summary_0029>>T h
  [[#index-T-h-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Hide the current (sub-)thread
  (=gnus-summary-hide-thread=).

-  <<index-T-S-_0028Summary_0029>>T S
  [[#index-T-S-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Expose all hidden threads
  (=gnus-summary-show-all-threads=).

-  <<index-T-H-_0028Summary_0029>>T H
  [[#index-T-H-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Hide all threads
  (=gnus-summary-hide-all-threads=).

-  <<index-T-t-_0028Summary_0029>>T t
  [[#index-T-t-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Re-thread the current article's
  thread (=gnus-summary-rethread-current=). This works even when the
  summary buffer is otherwise unthreaded.

-  <<index-T-_005e-_0028Summary_0029>>T ^
  [[#index-T-_005e-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Make the current article
  the child of the marked (or previous) article
  (=gnus-summary-reparent-thread=).

-  <<index-T-M_002d_005e-_0028Summary_0029>>T M-^
  [[#index-T-M_002d_005e-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Make the current
  article the parent of the marked articles
  (=gnus-summary-reparent-children=).

The following commands are thread movement commands. They all understand
the numeric prefix.

-  <<index-M_002dDOWN-_0028Summary_0029>>T n
  [[#index-M_002dDOWN-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] ::
- C-M-f ::
- M-DOWN :: Go to the next thread (=gnus-summary-next-thread=).

-  <<index-M_002dUP-_0028Summary_0029>>T p
  [[#index-M_002dUP-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] ::
- C-M-b ::
- M-UP :: Go to the previous thread (=gnus-summary-prev-thread=).

-  <<index-T-d-_0028Summary_0029>>T d
  [[#index-T-d-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Descend the thread
  (=gnus-summary-down-thread=).

-  <<index-T-u-_0028Summary_0029>>T u
  [[#index-T-u-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Ascend the thread
  (=gnus-summary-up-thread=).

-  <<index-T-o-_0028Summary_0029>>T o
  [[#index-T-o-_0028Summary_0029][¶]] :: Go to the top of the thread
  (=gnus-summary-top-thread=).

If you ignore subject while threading, you'll naturally end up with
threads that have several different subjects in them. If you then issue
a command like T k (=gnus-summary-kill-thread=) you might not wish to
kill the entire thread, but just those parts of the thread that have the
same subject as the current article. If you like this idea, you can
fiddle with =gnus-thread-operation-ignore-subject=. If it is non-=nil=
(which it is by default), subjects will be ignored when doing thread
commands. If this variable is =nil=, articles in the same thread with
different subjects will not be included in the operation in question. If
this variable is =fuzzy=, only articles that have subjects fuzzily equal
will be included (see [[#Fuzzy-Matching][Fuzzy Matching]]).
